newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK JAN-OCT 96 TRADE DEFICIT $15.39 BLN, UP 44.7.
newsitem.headline: TURK JAN-OCT 96 TRADE DEFICIT $15.39 BLN, UP 44.7.

text.p: Turkey's trade deficit jumped 44.7 percent in the first ten months of 1996 to $15.394 billion from 10.636 billion a year earlier, the State Statistics Institute (DIE) said on Friday.
Exports during the ten-month period climbed 8.6 percent year-on-year to $18.663 billion and imports jumped 22.4 percent to $34.057 billion, the DIE said in a statement.
The October trade deficit was up 11.0 percent from a year earlier at $1.416 billion. Exports in October rose 8.4 percent to $2.099 billion and imports climbed 9.4 percent to $3.515 billion.

The release of Turkish trade data for 1996 has been delayed because of technical difficulties arising from the country's customs union with the European Union which went into effect at the start of 1996.
The DIE has already begun releasing trade data for 1997.
In the first two months of this year, the trade deficit rose 12.6 percent from a year earlier to $2.597 billion.
